pages.text: Both blocks only accept $(item)carbon dioxide$() and release it into the air with a puff of smoke. They work for fireboxes, engines, coke ovens and anything else that makes CO2.

$(l)Exhaust$()$(li)Holds $(item)1000 mB$() and can face any direction.$(li)Vents $(item)10 mB per tick$() (200 mB per second).$(li)When less than 300 mB of room is left, it vents $(item)100 mB per tick$() instead.$(br2)So an exhaust kept nearly full can vent a lot: enough for the biggest firebox.

$(l)Smokestacks$()$(br)Brick, concrete and metal smokestacks all work the same way and only differ in looks.$(li)Each holds $(item)8000 mB$().$(li)Stack them: each block passes its CO2 up to the one above, and only the $(item)top$() one vents.

$(li)The top vents $(item)10 mB per tick$(), or $(item)50 mB per tick$() when less than 1000 mB of room is left.$(br2)Smokestacks make a big buffer and a nice chimney. For a busy factory, feed several stacks or add exhausts next to them.
Carbon dioxide also has uses: 1000 mB fills a $(item)fire extinguisher$() or a $(item)carbon dioxide tank$() in a spout.
